body:
CANNOT CLOSE THE BLEND BEAD YET - there is a new candidate on it, 460a14a, and it is a defect in the
work you just merged. Your close instruction was written at 20:54Z; I posted the candidate at 21:12Z.
Full detail is in the decision note on the bead and in the DM I sent you and scout. Short version:

chartEligible tested node.evidence, but the Chart term is produced by ChartDistance.reduction, which
measures over view.structuralMembers(node.ref) - the LEAVES. node.evidence is the contract of
ChartDistance.report, a DIFFERENT function with no view parameter. The predicate was written to the
wrong function. They agree on a leaf and diverge on a segment, and StorySourceView guarantees the
divergence: segments never get a fabricated chart. So Chart came out present-but-not-eligible,
wPresent exceeded wEligible, and both halves failed the same direction - the blend multiplied the
cost DOWN (0.9054 against a correct 1.0405, so 14.9% low) while supportOf's min(1.0,_) clamp
reported the over-unity ratio as flat 1.0 full support. Measured on sc2/e4, not argued.
Seven-module gate green, and NOT ONE expected value moved, which is the prediction the
"coincides on leaves" argument makes.

HOLDS, since you said nobody can see intent from a bare reserve_open: I have released hsmm.scala
from rv-01M17M70JNTR5M0G2GXM6QTFKP. I now hold exactly the two files 460a14a touches - CostSuite.scala
on that rv, cost.scala on rv-01M17N8HH49AH9NQTK2MV4CS0T - both on this bead. Nothing else.

YOUR ENFORCEABILITY QUESTION, RE-DERIVED AGAINST WHAT LANDED. You were right that my draft rule no
longer holds, but not because the invariant moved - because ITS SUBJECT STOPPED EXISTING. I proposed
asserting that for every term in MayBeMissing the imputed value times its weight is zero. After
eligible-set scaling there is no imputed value to zero out: an absent eligible term is simply not in
`terms`, and its weight is carried by the scale factor instead. The law would now be vacuously true
in the worst way - passing because it describes machinery that was deleted. That is the same failure
shape as my Law 2, and I would rather say so than quietly rewrite it into something adjacent.

THE INVARIANT THAT ACTUALLY HOLDS NOW IS CONTAINMENT: present must be a subset of eligible. It is
what makes the two published quantities mean anything - scale >= 1 (measuring more never lowers a
price) and support <= 1 (the fraction of eligible weight actually measured). Today's defect is
exactly a containment violation, so this is not a hypothetical.

And it is currently UNENFORCED IN THE ONE PLACE THAT SEES IT. supportOf clamps with min(1.0, _).
The over-unity ratio WAS the evidence of the bug, and the clamp deleted it before anyone could read
it. A cell where present exceeds eligible is incoherent by construction, not merely unusual, so the
honest behaviour is to refuse rather than clamp. That is a ruling for you, not a change I will make
unasked, because it decides whether cost() can fail: either supportOf returns Either and cost()
propagates, or it stays total and the containment check moves to a law over cost()'s own two sets.
I lean to the second - keep cost() total, assert containment in align's laws where it can be checked
for every fixture cell rather than only where a suite happens to look. Say which and I will build it.

ON YOUR TWO THINGS. Recorded, and the second one matters more than the first. What I take from the
pattern you named - that this defect class is invisible to suites by construction, because a value
meaning "we could not measure" is indistinguishable to a test from one meaning "we measured this" -
is that the review chain is not overhead on top of the gate, it is the only instrument that detects
this class at all. Today's finding came from reading my own carrier and asking what the numbers
would look like if the predicate were wrong. That is a habit I got from being stopped twice.
